tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Company has received an order from the CIT(A) issued under section 250 of the Act for the assessment year 2020-21. The order has been passed pursuant to appeal filed by the Company against the intimation issued under section 143(1) of the Act for the captioned year. In the said intimation, erroneous addition of Rs. 13.11 crore was made by CPC. In the captioned order, the CIT(A) has directed the Assessing Officer to delete the addition made by CPC, post verifying the claim of the Company. An appeal was filed before CIT(A) against which the CIT(A) has passed the captioned order. Now, the Company would take up the matter with the Assessing Officer to pass the order in line with the directions provided by the CIT(A).
tax_litigation.status: The estimated favorable tax impact on account of the captioned CIT(A) order would be Rs. 3.30 crore (approx.).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Company has received a final assessment order from the Assessment Unit being passed under section 143(3) read with section 144C(13) and 144(B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for assessment year 2022-23, wherein adjustment on the legacy transfer pricing and corporate tax issues have been proposed. The matter will be challenged before the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) by filing an appeal.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has challenged the matter before the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) by filing an appeal.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Company has received an appeal order for the financial year 2018-19, wherein certain adjustments initially made by the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax Investigation relating to supplies made by the Company under Patient Access Program, have been upheld by the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal). The order was passed by the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal). The matter will be challenged before the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) by filing an appeal.
tax_litigation.status: Matter will be suitably challenged in due course. The expected overall financial implication cannot be determined at this stage.

operating_notes.text: Received CDSCO approval on May 20, 2026 to import Calquence 100 mg for untreated mantle cell lymphoma in combination with BR for ASCT-ineligible patients.
Received 11 regulatory approvals from CDSCO for new medicines and indications in FY26.
FY26 therapy-wise revenue: Oncology ₹1,610.09 Cr, Biopharmaceuticals ₹524.32 Cr, Rare Disease ₹21.46 Cr.
Manufacturing site operations ceased in the quarter ended 30 June 2025; assets are classified as held for sale pending a buyer.
A ₹278.3 million provision for past service cost on gratuity and compensated absences was recognised under the new Labour Codes.
Surrendered factory license to the Department of Factories for cancellation following manufacturing site exit.
Received tax appeal order from Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal) for FY2018-19 involving ₹9.24 Cr (excluding interest and penalty) relating to Patient Access Program supplies.

timeline.summary: Shareholders approved shifting of the registered office from Karnataka to Maharashtra with 99.99% majority via postal ballot.
Received CDSCO permission to import and distribute Calquence (Acalabrutinib) for untreated mantle cell lymphoma.
AstraZeneca Pharma India reported FY26 revenue of ₹2,275.58 Cr (+33% YoY) and PAT of ₹187.52 Cr, highlighting 11 regulatory approvals during the year.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹578.61 Cr (+20.4% YoY), net profit ₹44.88 Cr (-23.0% YoY).
AstraZeneca Pharma India surrendered its factory license for cancellation on June 3, 2026.
AstraZeneca Pharma received an appeal order from the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax upholding a ₹9.24 Cr adjustment for FY2018-19.
NSE Sustainability Ratings assigned AstraZeneca Pharma an ESG score of 73 for FY26.

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited’s shareholders approved Mr. Arun Krishna’s appointment as Non-Executive Director and Ms. Bhavana Agrawal’s designation change to Non-Executive Director via postal ballot on October 14, 2026.
